summary: Reading a whole Canvas list, and the course snapshot built on top of it. internal/client/client.go's doInternal now also returns the final response's http.Header; do() and doRead() keep their three-value shape and drop it, so none of the 25 generated call sites change, and a new hand-authored doWithHeader() keeps it. internal/client/pages.go is hand-authored and holds GetAll, which adds per_page=100, follows Link: <...>; rel="next", and returns every item or no items at all; splitLinks and parseLink read the header, ignoring the rel="last" and rel="prev" beside it. internal/coursesnapshot/snapshot.go mirrors checks/src/types.ts field for field and holds Marshal, which encodes with SetEscapeHTML(false). internal/coursesnapshot/build.go reads a course into that shape from seven paths, all under /api/v1/courses/<id>. internal/sandbox/messages.go gains MsgTooManyPages and MsgNoTimeZone, plus NotTheCanvasRead for a next page pointing at another server.
reason:
Canvas answers a collection a page at a time and says where the rest is only in a Link header, so a reader that takes the first answer gets a course with its first hundred pages in it. Everything downstream is a check, so that would surface as a clean report on a course nobody fully looked at. GetAll is therefore all-or-nothing: any page failing is returned as an error with no items, because a caller cannot tell a short list from a complete one, and a Canvas that keeps promising one more page stops at 100 pages with ErrTooManyPages rather than handing back a list missing the rest.

The address of the next page comes out of an answer, so it is checked like any other address Canvas hands over. Twice: once by the client's general rule, which inside Canvas Builder refuses anything that isn't the gateway and gives the agent the gateway's own wording, and once by a scheme-and-host comparison against the Canvas this CLI was pointed at, which holds in every mode. Neither message repeats the address itself, only its scheme and host: the rest of a Canvas address can carry a verifier, which is a credential. An address that doesn't parse fails the same way, with the same sentence.

GetAll goes through the transport rather than through Get, because the response cache is keyed on path and params: paging through it could answer one page from an older read and splice two different reads together. The next page is passed as a path with its query already attached and nil params, because a map[string]string cannot carry the repeated include[] keys Canvas writes into its own Link addresses.

Marshal exists because json.Marshal escapes '<', '>' and '&'. The checks read HTML, so the default encoder would change what they see, roughly triple a real course's snapshot, and leave a document nobody can read by hand. A course taught in Arabic or French has to arrive exactly as Canvas sent it.

Build's request order is not arbitrary: assignments are read before discussion topics, because a graded topic takes its three dates from the assignment behind it, and that assignment is itself left out of the snapshot (Canvas lists a graded discussion and a classic quiz as assignments too, and the checks would otherwise report the same item twice). The unfiltered list is kept for exactly that lookup. A course with no time_zone is an error rather than a snapshot, because every date in a course is written in the course's own zone and the dates check has nothing to judge against without it.
known_limitations:
Plan E has Build set c.NoCache = true. It doesn't: the course is read with GetNoCache and the seven lists through GetAll, which never touches the cache at all, so nothing cached reaches a snapshot without Build switching caching off for the rest of the run on a client its caller also uses for other things. The plan's intent is met; its mechanism is not.

The 100-page cap is on pages, not items. It is 10,000 items only because GetAll asks for per_page=100; a Canvas that ignores per_page and answers 10 at a time would stop at 1,000. The message states the 10,000 figure, so in that case it would overstate what was read.

A graded discussion whose assignment_id names an assignment that isn't in the assignment list is graded with all three dates null. That would be a course Canvas is contradicting itself about, and the dates check reports a graded item with no dates rather than this failing outright.

Nothing here reads a New Quiz's questions. The stand-in is recognised only by the title the quiz builder writes, so a stand-in an instructor has renamed is snapshotted as an ordinary assignment, and its questions are reported as checked when nothing looked at them. Decision D5 accepts this.

Files carry only id and display_name, so no check can look inside a course's files. That is what checks/src/types.ts asks for; the import check in canvas-builder-v2 is what reads file contents.

GetAll holds every item of one list in memory at once. At the cap that is 10,000 raw JSON objects, which is fine for a course and would not be for an account-wide list, and nothing here reads one.

A dry run returns ErrDryRun from the first page rather than a list, because the dry-run envelope isn't an array and the request was printed instead of sent. A caller wanting to show what a snapshot would ask for has to print the requests, not read the answer.
validated_outcome:
go build ./... and go vet ./... clean. go test ./... passing across every package on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1, exit 0, including internal/sandbox's TestMessagesAvoidForbiddenWords and TestGatewayMessagesMatchV2 with the two new messages in place. go test -race ./internal/client/ ./internal/coursesnapshot/ passing. golangci-lint run --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 reports nothing on internal/client/pages.go, internal/client/pages_test.go, internal/coursesnapshot/ or internal/sandbox/; the touched generated file reports only its pre-existing findings. gofmt -l clean on every hand-authored file in this patch.

New coverage. internal/client/pages_test.go: TestGetAllFollowsLinks reads 250 items over three pages and asserts the count, the first and last id, exactly three requests, and per_page=100 on each. TestGetAllFailsOnAnyPage answers 500 on page 2 and asserts both an error and that no items came back with it. TestGetAllRefusesNextOffGateway points the next link at a second local server inside Canvas Builder and asserts the gateway's wording with that server seeing no connection. TestGetAllRefusesNextOffBaseURLOutsideCanvasBuilder asserts the same rule holds with no gateway in play. TestGetAllStopsAtTheCap answers with a next link forever and asserts ErrTooManyPages after exactly 100 requests. TestGetAllSaysSoOnADryRun asserts ErrDryRun.

internal/coursesnapshot/build_test.go: TestBuildMapsCanvasToSnapshot builds a synthetic course with one page, a plain assignment, a New Quiz stand-in, a quiz-backed assignment, a classic quiz, a graded and an ungraded discussion, one announcement and one file, and compares the marshalled JSON against the whole expected snapshot written inline, then asserts both include[] parameters were sent. TestBuildKeepsNonEnglishText asserts an Arabic page body and the title Lecon 1 survive in the struct and in the JSON, and that the output contains no \\u003c, \\u003e, \\u0026 or \\u00e7. TestBuildEmptyCourseUsesEmptyLists asserts all six lists encode as []. TestBuildNeedsTimeZone asserts the exact message. TestBuildUsesCourseScopedPathsOnly asserts every recorded request is a GET under /api/v1/courses/7. TestSnapshotAcceptedByCbChecks runs the real node checks/src/cli.ts all --snapshot - on the built snapshot and asserts exit 0 with a dates report; it passed against canvas-builder-v2 at 678f8a4 on node v22.23.3 and skips without CANVAS_BUILDER_V2 or node.

CodeRabbit reviewed the patch (uncommitted plus untracked, all seven files) and reported no findings.
